title: Report RP-74: Syrian rue, acacia bark and ephedrine
epigraph: “No self-introduction. I am whoever you think I am. That is up to you, not me.”
source: Retold in full from FreeODwiki report RP-74, with the person’s private details left out and the report’s mistakes pointed out.

sections.heading: Spring风
paragraphs: That line was the first thing Spring风 ever posted, on 4 June 2022. The name means spring wind. Seven months later they were dead, at nineteen.
In between they became one of the first people an online drug-use community went to with its questions. They filled sheets of scrap paper with chemical structures and posted them.

They posted the small things too. That it was raining, and that the rain suited the day. That there was a cat in a shop they passed, and it was cute. That the rain began whenever they left the umbrella upstairs, and stopped as soon as they went back for it.

They lost their temper and hated themselves for it. They wished they could be alone in the house. A friend wrote them a note about that temper, and they broke the promise they made in return, and wanted to say sorry ten thousand times. The friend was not angry, only sad, and that was harder.

Once, in one of the rages that came after DXM, they set out meaning to end their life. The feeling fell away as suddenly as it had come, and they went home, puzzled at themselves. They had told themselves before that a poor life is better than a good death.
A friend remembers the entrance exam of 2022: Spring风 said hello and went in on DXM and caffeine lozenges. Nobody ever found out what they heard in the English listening test.

sections.heading: 8 January 2023
paragraphs: At 6:15 in the morning they put Syrian rue seeds on to boil. The seeds hold harmala alkaloids, an MAOI. At 2:33 in the afternoon they swallowed 24 asthma tablets whose ingredients include ephedrine.

The acacia bark had come at noon, bought online. With the ephedrine still working they took out about 20 g and got it wet by accident, so they began again with a fresh portion and broke it up by hand until their hands bled. They were worn out. It went into the pot with the rue and boiled for more than an hour and a half.
At 7:47 pm they drank it in one go. By 8:11 the world they knew had come apart: they were badly confused, with intense and frightening hallucinations.

The knives had not been put away, and in the delirium they hurt themselves. Their father felt that something was wrong and ran in. They were resuscitated for a long time. They could not be saved. The cause of death was given as multiple organ failure from poisoning.
The funeral was in February. The report ends its account of the day with one line: they turned into wind, and went with the wind.

sections.heading: What made that day deadly
paragraphs: None of it was fate. Every part of that day has a reason, and every reason is something the rest of us can learn.

An MAOI with ephedrine. Harmala alkaloids stop the body breaking down ephedrine and the noradrenaline it releases. Blood pressure can climb into a hypertensive crisis: bleeding in the brain, burst blood vessels, heart failure. The report names this as the main cause. The small amount of opioid in the tablets was not the main danger.

Acacia bark with an MAOI. Some acacia species hold 5-MeO-DMT as well as DMT, and the bark seldom says which species it is. 5-MeO-DMT with an MAOI is one of the most dangerous combinations there is. Boiling for a long time draws out more of whatever the bark holds.
Unknown plant material. Bark sold online may have been sprayed with pesticides, which the report thinks sped the poisoning.
No one beside them, and sharp things left out. A sober person in the room, and the knives put away beforehand, might have prevented the injuries.

sections.heading: What the old notes got wrong
paragraphs: On their second day in the community they wrote, on scrap paper, that caffeine is an MAOI and that a lot of caffeine with harmala alkaloids is "about the same as MDMA". Both are wrong. Caffeine is not a meaningful MAOI, and an MAOI with stimulants is the very kind of mix that raised blood pressure here. Don't act on those notes.

They also wrote that DXM builds no tolerance, gave 48 tablets as the most to take at once, and said overdosing on caffeine was the better choice. None of it holds. Tolerance to DXM does build, 48 tablets is already a heavy overdose, and caffeine in overdose can stop a heart.

The DXM diary is the hardest part to read. It goes minute by minute: unsteady on their feet, unable to remember where they had put the thermometer, asking whether their home was their home. Then days of anger. Then, at two in the morning, a warning for everyone else, the same sentence three times over: don't keep overdosing on DXM. They were someone who wrote things down, and who could say when they had been wrong.

sections.heading: For whoever comes after
paragraphs: Never mix an MAOI (Syrian rue, ayahuasca, harmala alkaloids, moclobemide and the like) with ephedrine, pseudoephedrine, cold or asthma tablets, amphetamines, MDMA, DXM, SSRIs or 5-MeO-DMT. Let at least a full day pass between them, either way round.
Don't brew plant material when you don't know the species or where it came from.
Have a sober sitter, and put knives and sharp things away before you start.
A pounding headache, chest pain, confusion, a racing heart or a high temperature after a mix like this is an emergency. Call an ambulance and say what was taken.
You are allowed to be tired. School, work, everything pressing down: wanting one night away from your own head is human. Just be here when the blossom comes. We are all Spring风.

summary: Spring风 died in January 2023, at 19, after 24 ephedrine asthma tablets and a home brew of Syrian rue and acacia bark. Who they were, what happened that day, why it was deadly, and what to carry forward.
